data.name: Zelophehad
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew words 'zel' (God) and 'phehad' (secret). This name was given to a son of Hepher, one of the heads of the families of Manasseh. It signifies God's hidden or secret plan or protection.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that reminds us of God's divine plan and protection.
data.numerology_meaning: Creative, artistic, and empathetic individuals, they have a strong need for self-expression.

in_hebrew.name: צלפחד
in_hebrew.meaning: בן-זמן, בן-אזמון, בן-בכור, בן-ארץ, משמעות: יסוד-בקע-האדמה, קשר-לבב
in_hebrew.long_meaning: צלפחד הוא שם משפחה עברי שמקורו בברית החדשה (יוחנן 7:11). סוגיות תאולוגיות והיסטוריות: שמו של צלפחד, בנו של חצירון, שהיה נכדו של יוסף, ואביו של מוכי, שהיה נכד של מנשה, שהיה תושב- כנען (מקרא, 7:11).

in_greek.name: Ζελωφεδ
in_greek.meaning: ὁ υἱός τοῦ Ἀζωμόν, ὁ υἱός τοῦ Ἀζμόν, ὁ υἱός τοῦ Ἐκκλησίας, ὁ υἱός τοῦ Ἰσραήλ, ἡ ἐξήγηση: ἡ ἔνωσις-τοῦ-ἀνθρώπου, ἡ ἔνωσις-τοῦ-θεοῦ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ζελωφεδ (Ζελωφεδ ὁ Ἰουδαῖος) ἐστὶ ἄνθρωπος τῆς Ἰουδαίας, ὃν εἶδεν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ ἐποίησε τὸ ἅγιον ὕδωρ (Ἰωάννης 7:11). Ἡ ἀγωγή τῆς Ὀρθοδοξίας: Ζελωφεδ, ὁ φίλος τοῦ Ἰησοῦ, ὁ ἔχων τὴν ἔνωσιν τοῦ θεοῦ, εἶναι ἕνα ἔξαγμα τοῦ ἡμέτερου πνευματικῆς ἀναζητήσεως.

in_latin.name: Zelophehad
in_latin.meaning: filius Azemonis, filius Azemonis, filius Ecclesiae, filius Israel, significatio: coniunctio-hominis, coniunctio-dei
in_latin.long_meaning: Zelophehad, filius Azemonis, qui apparuit Iesu Christo, et in quo fecit miraculum (Ioannes 7:11). Historia Ecclesiae: Zelophehad, amicus Iesu, qui habuit conjunctionem Dei, est exemplum nostrae spiritualis investigationis.

in_english.name: Zelophehad
in_english.meaning: son of Zelophehad, son of Azmon, son of Zimri, son of Phinehas, meaning: connection-birth, connection-God
in_english.long_meaning: Zelophehad is a biblical name derived from Hebrew roots, meaning connection or joining with God. Etymological context: Zelophehad was a son of Zelophehad, a grandson of Manasseh, a son of Joseph, and a descendant of Jacob (Numbers 27:3). Historical significance: The Zelophehads were known for their faithfulness and their connection to the divine. In the New Testament, Jesus performed a miracle in the presence of Zelophehad, demonstrating the power of faith and the connection between God and humanity (John 7:11).

biblical_reference.note: Zelophehad is mentioned in the book of Numbers as a leader among the Israelites and as a son of Zelophehad, a grandson of Manasseh, a son of Joseph, and a descendant of Jacob.

saint_reference.note: Zelophehad is not the name of a recognized saint in the Catholic or Orthodox Church.

data.cultural_impact: The name Zelophehad is mentioned only once in the Bible in the Book of Numbers 26:33. However, the story of Zelophehad and his daughters gaining an inheritance in the land of Canaan set an important precedent in Jewish and later Western legal systems, recognizing the rights of women and setting the stage for the concept of primogeniture (the inheritance rights of the eldest son).
data.spiritual_significance: The name Zelophehad holds deep spiritual significance for Christians, representing trust and faith in God's mysterious ways and plans for our lives. It is a reminder that even when things may seem hidden or unclear, God is working behind the scenes, and His plans are ultimately good and perfect. Moreover, Zelophehad's courage and determination in challenging the traditional expectations of inheritance laws and carving out a place for himself and his family within the community of Israel can be seen as a model of faithfulness and perseverance.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Sarah Zelophehad in Athens, Greece credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Zelophehad, which means "God's secret". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
